“Matches an element in a state.”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>A. <code>:last-of-type</code></li><li>B. <code>:required / :optional</code></li><li>✔ C. <code>:</code></li><li>D. <code>~</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p1623">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 1624 / 8000 · Practice 4</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p1625">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p1625" data-page="1625" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 748"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 4</span><span>Page 1625 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 748 — h1 × padding-left</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">h1</span> <span class="badge prop">padding-left</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">padding-left</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;h1&gt;</code> — a section heading of importance level 1 (h1 = highest). Inner space at the left.</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;h1&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><div style="font-weight:700;font-size:23.5px;line-height:1.25;margin:2px 0">Heading level 1</div></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;h1&gt;Heading level 1&lt;/h1&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>padding-left</b> = <b>length</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>h1 { padding-left: length; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">What does this selector do? “Focus via keyboard (not mouse click).”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>✔ A. <code>:focus-visible</code></li><li>B. <code>:is(sel, …)</code></li><li>C. <code>:in-range / :out-of-range</code></li><li>D. <code>::first-letter</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p1624">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 1625 / 8000 · Practice 4</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p1626">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p1626" data-page="1626" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 749"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 4</span><span>Page 1626 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 749 — hr × outline-offset</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">hr</span> <span class="badge prop">outline-offset</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">outline-offset</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;hr&gt;</code> — a thematic break between paragraphs (scene change, topic shift). Distance between the outline and the element edge.</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;hr&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><div style="font-size:13px"><p style="margin:0 0 6px">Before the break.</p><hr style="border:none;border-top:2px solid #d1d5db;margin:8px 0"><p style="margin:0">After the break.</p></div></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;p&gt;Before the break.&lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;p&gt;After the break.&lt;/p&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>outline-offset</b> = <b>length</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>hr { outline-offset: length; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">What does this selector do? “Last child of its parent.”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>✔ A. <code>:last-child</code></li><li>B. <code>:checked</code></li><li>C. <code>:dir(dir)</code></li><li>D. <code>::placeholder</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p1625">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 1626 / 8000 · Practice 4</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p1627">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p1627" data-page="1627" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 750"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 4</span><span>Page 1627 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 750 — dialog × overflow-y</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">dialog</span> <span class="badge prop">overflow-y</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">overflow-y</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;dialog&gt;</code> — a native dialog box: modal when shown with showmodal(), non-modal when shown with show(). Vertical overflow behavior.</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;dialog&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><div style="width:240px;background:#fff;border:1px solid #d1d5db;border-radius:10px;box-shadow:0 8px 24px rgba(0,0,0,.18);padding:14px;font-size:13px"><b>Are you sure?</b><div style="margin-top:10px;text-align:right"><button style="border:1px solid #d1d5db;background:#f9fafb;border-radius:6px;padding:4px 10px;margin-right:6px;font-size:12px">Cancel</button><button style="border:none;background:#2563eb;color:#fff;border-radius:6px;padding:4px 12px;font-size:12px">OK</button></div></div></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;dialog id=&quot;dlg&quot;&gt; &lt;form method=&quot;dialog&quot;&gt; &lt;p&gt;Are you sure?&lt;/p&gt; &lt;button value=&quot;cancel&quot;&gt;Cancel&lt;/button&gt; &lt;button formnovalidate&gt;OK&lt;/button&gt; &lt;/form&gt; &lt;/dialog&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>overflow-y</b> = <b>keyword</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>dialog { overflow-y: keyword; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">What does this selector do? “The n-th child OF ITS TAG type (ignores other tags).”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>A. <code>:valid / :invalid</code></li><li>✔ B. <code>:nth-of-type(n)</code></li><li>C. <code>+</code></li><li>D. <code>::file-selector-button</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p1626">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 1627 / 8000 · Practice 4</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p1628">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p1628" data-page="1628" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 751"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 4</span><span>Page 1628 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 751 — s × align-items</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">s</span> <span class="badge prop">align-items</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">align-items</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;s&gt;</code> — marks text that is no longer accurate or relevant (not a strikethrough for style). Aligns flex items along the cross axis (for all items).</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;s&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><p style="margin:0;font-size:13px">Price: <s style="color:#9ca3af">$99</s> <b>$79</b></p></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;p&gt;Price: &lt;s&gt;$99&lt;/s&gt; $79&lt;/p&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>align-items</b> = <b>stretch</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>s { align-items: stretch; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">What does this selector do? “No children at all (not even text).”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>A. <code>:target</code></li><li>B. <code>::after</code></li><li>C. <code>element</code></li><li>✔ D. <code>:empty</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p1627">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 1628 / 8000 · Practice 4</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p1629">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p1629" data-page="1629" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 752"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 4</span><span>Page 1629 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 752 — dfn × grid-template-areas</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">dfn</span> <span class="badge prop">grid-template-areas</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">grid-template-areas</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;dfn&gt;</code> — the term being defined on the page. Names grid regions with an ASCII map — the most readable layout syntax.</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;dfn&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><p style="margin:0;font-size:13px"><dfn style="font-style:italic"><b>semantics</b></dfn>: the meaning carried by markup, not just its appearance.</p></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;p&gt;&lt;dfn&gt;semantics&lt;/dfn&gt;: the meaning of markup.&lt;/p&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>grid-template-areas</b> = <b>…</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>dfn { grid-template-areas: …; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">What does this selector do? “Like :is but with ZERO specificity.”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>A. <code>&gt;</code></li><li>B. <code>::selection</code></li><li>C. <code>[attr]</code></li><li>✔ D. <code>:where(sel, …)</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p1628">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 1629 / 8000 · Practice 4</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p1630">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p1630" data-page="1630" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 753"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 4</span><span>Page 1630 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 753 — sup × font</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">sup</span> <span class="badge prop">font</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">font</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;sup&gt;</code> — superscript text (rendered above the baseline). Shorthand: font-style font-variant font-weight font-size/line-height font-family.</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;sup&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><p style="margin:0;font-size:13px">E = mc<sup>2</sup></p></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;p&gt;E = mc&lt;sup&gt;2&lt;/sup&gt;&lt;/p&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>font</b> = <b>…</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>sup { font: …; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">What does this selector do? “Form control usable or not.”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>✔ A. <code>:enabled / :disabled</code></li><li>B. <code>~</code></li><li>C. <code>::backdrop</code></li><li>D. <code>[attr$=…]</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p1629">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 1630 / 8000 · Practice 4</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p1631">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p1631" data-page="1631" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 754"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 4</span><span>Page 1631 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 754 — ol × letter-spacing</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">ol</span> <span class="badge prop">letter-spacing</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">letter-spacing</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;ol&gt;</code> — a numbered list of items. Space between letters (tracking).</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;ol&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><ol start="2" style="font-size:13px;margin:0;padding-left:22px;line-height:1.7"><li>Second step</li><li>Third step</li></ol></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;ol start=&quot;2&quot;&gt; &lt;li&gt;Second step&lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt;Third step&lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ol&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>letter-spacing</b> = <b>length</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>ol { letter-spacing: length; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">What does this selector do? “The placeholder is currently visible (field empty).”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>A. <code>::first-letter</code></li><li>B. <code>*</code></li><li>✔ C. <code>:placeholder-shown</code></li><li>D. <code>:hover</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p1630">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 1631 / 8000 · Practice 4</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p1632">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p1632" data-page="1632" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 755"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 4</span><span>Page 1632 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 755 — source × vertical-align</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">source</span> <span class="badge prop">vertical-align</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">vertical-align</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;source&gt;</code> — a candidate resource for &lt;video&gt;, &lt;audio&gt; or &lt;picture&gt;. Aligns inline content to the baseline (icons with text!).</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;source&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><div style="font-family:monospace;font-size:11px;background:#f6f8fa;border:1px solid #d0d7de;border-radius:6px;padding:8px">1) movie.webm ✓ plays<br>2) movie.mp4 (fallback, skipped)</div></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;video controls&gt; &lt;source src=&quot;movie.webm&quot; type=&quot;video/webm&quot;&gt; &lt;source src=&quot;movie.mp4&quot; type=&quot;video/mp4&quot;&gt; &lt;/video&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>vertical-align</b> = <b>middle</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>source { vertical-align: middle; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">What does this selector do? “Element&#x27;s language matches the code.”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>A. <code>::placeholder</code></li><li>B. <code>#id</code></li><li>C. <code>:active</code></li><li>✔ D. <code>:lang(code)</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p1631">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 1632 / 8000 · Practice 4</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p1633">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p1633" data-page="1633" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 756"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 4</span><span>Page 1633 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 756 — iframe × background</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">iframe</span> <span class="badge prop">background</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">background</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;iframe&gt;</code> — embeds another html page in a nested browsing context. Shorthand: color + image + position + size + repeat + attachment + origin + clip.</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;iframe&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><div style="border:2px solid #8b949e;border-radius:6px;width:250px;padding:8px;background:#fff"><h1 style="font-size:14px;margin:2px 0 0">Hello from an iframe</h1><div style="font-size:10px;color:#8b949e">separate document, own DOM</div></div></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;iframe srcdoc=&quot;&lt;h1&gt;Hello from an iframe&lt;/h1&gt;&quot; width=&quot;260&quot; height=&quot;70&quot; sandbox=&quot;allow-same-origin&quot;&gt;&lt;/iframe&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>background</b> = <b>linear-gradient(90deg,#2563eb,#7c3aed)</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>iframe { background: linear-gradient(90deg,#2563eb,#7c3aed); }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">What does this selector do? “Any depth descendant.”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>✔ A. <code>descendant (space)</code></li><li>B. <code>::file-selector-button</code></li><li>C. <code>[attr^=…]</code></li><li>D. <code>:only-child</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p1632">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 1633 / 8000 · Practice 4</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p1634">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p1634" data-page="1634" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 757"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 4</span><span>Page 1634 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 757 — input × forced-color-adjust</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">input</span> <span class="badge prop">forced-color-adjust</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">forced-color-adjust</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;input&gt;</code> — the most versatile form control: text, email, number, date, file, checkbox, radio, range, color, search and more. Whether the OS &#x27;forced colors&#x27; mode (Windows High Contrast) overrides colors.</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;input&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><form style="display:grid;gap:8px;font-size:12px;max-width:250px"><label style="display:grid;gap:3px"><b>Full name</b><input style="border:1px solid #d1d5db;border-radius:6px;padding:5px 8px"></label><label style="display:grid;gap:3px"><b>Email</b><input type="email" style="border:1px solid #d1d5db;border-radius:6px;padding:5px 8px"></label><label style="display:flex;gap:6px;align-items:center"><input type="checkbox" checked> Newsletter</label><button style="justify-self:start;background:#2563eb;color:#fff;border:none;border-radius:6px;padding:6px 16px">Send</button></form></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;form&gt; &lt;label&gt;Full name &lt;input type=&quot;text&quot; name=&quot;name&quot; required autocomplete=&quot;name&quot;&gt; &lt;/label&gt; &lt;label&gt;Email &lt;input type=&quot;email&quot; name=&quot;email&quot; required&gt; &lt;/label&gt; &lt;label&gt;Age &lt;input type=&quot;number&quot; name=&quot;age&quot; min=&quot;0&quot; max=&quot;120&quot;&gt; &lt;/label&gt; &lt;label&gt;&lt;input type=&quot;checkbox&quot; name=&quot;news&quot; checked&gt; Newsletter&lt;/label&gt; &lt;button&gt;Send&lt;/button&gt; &lt;/form&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>forced-color-adjust</b> = <b>…</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>input { forced-color-adjust: …; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">What does this selector do? “Generated content INSIDE the start of the element.”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>A. <code>element</code></li><li>B. <code>:</code></li><li>C. <code>:first-of-type</code></li><li>✔ D. <code>::before</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p1633">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 1634 / 8000 · Practice 4</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p1635">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p1635" data-page="1635" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 758"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 4</span><span>Page 1635 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 758 — label × list-style-position</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">label</span> <span class="badge prop">list-style-position</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">list-style-position</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;label&gt;</code> — a caption for a form control — clickable, and read by screen readers. }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">Which element is described by: “Marks text that is no longer accurate or relevant (not a strikethrough for style).”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>✔ A. <code>&lt;s&gt;</code></li><li>B. <code>&lt;object&gt;</code></li><li>C. <code>&lt;ins&gt;</code></li><li>D. <code>&lt;samp&gt;</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p1683">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 1684 / 8000 · Practice 5</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p1685">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p1685" data-page="1685" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 808"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 5</span><span>Page 1685 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 808 — bdi × transform-box</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">bdi</span> <span class="badge prop">transform-box</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">transform-box</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;bdi&gt;</code> — isolates text so its direction does not affect surrounding text. }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">Which element is described by: “Defines a client-side image map: clickable regions on an image.”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>A. <code>&lt;isindex&gt;</code></li><li>✔ B. <code>&lt;map&gt;</code></li><li>C. <code>&lt;b&gt;</code></li><li>D. <code>&lt;label&gt;</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p1696">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 1697 / 8000 · Practice 5</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p1698">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p1698" data-page="1698" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 821"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 5</span><span>Page 1698 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 821 — h4 × touch-action</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">h4</span> <span class="badge prop">touch-action</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">touch-action</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;h4&gt;</code> — a section heading of importance level 4 (h1 = highest). Distance to the right of the element.</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;samp&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><p style="margin:0;font-size:13px">If you see <samp style="font-family:monospace;background:#fef2f2;color:#b91c1c;padding:1px 5px;border-radius:4px;font-size:12px">404 Not Found</samp>, the page is missing.</p></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;p&gt;If you see &lt;samp&gt;404 Not Found&lt;/samp&gt;, the page is missing.&lt;/p&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>margin-right</b> = <b>length</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>samp { margin-right: length; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">Which element is described by: “The title/caption of a &lt;table&gt;.”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>A. <code>&lt;script&gt;</code></li><li>✔ B. <code>&lt;caption&gt;</code></li><li>C. <code>&lt;samp&gt;</code></li><li>D. <code>&lt;center&gt;</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p1701">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 1702 / 8000 · Practice 5</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p1703">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p1703" data-page="1703" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 826"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 5</span><span>Page 1703 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 826 — rp × border-width</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">rp</span> <span class="badge prop">border-width</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">border-width</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;rp&gt;</code> — fallback parentheses for ruby annotations in browsers without ruby support. Whether the text can be selected by the user.</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;em&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><p style="margin:0;font-size:13px">I love <em>you</em>. — <i>em changes who is stressed</i></p></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;p&gt;I love &lt;em&gt;you&lt;/em&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>user-select</b> = <b>none</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>em { user-select: none; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">What does this selector do? “Direct children only.”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>A. <code>::backdrop</code></li><li>B. <code>[attr=value]</code></li><li>✔ C. <code>&gt;</code></li><li>D. <code>:last-child</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p1790">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 1791 / 8000 · Practice 5</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p1792">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p1792" data-page="1792" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 915"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 5</span><span>Page 1792 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 915 — abbr × field-sizing</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">abbr</span> <span class="badge prop">field-sizing</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">field-sizing</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;abbr&gt;</code> — an abbreviation or acronym, with its expansion in the title attribute. Let an input/textarea size itself to its content (content-based width).</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;abbr&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><p style="margin:0;font-size:13px"><abbr title="Hypertext Markup Language" style="text-decoration:underline dotted;cursor:help">HTML</abbr> — hover me for the tooltip</p></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;abbr title=&quot;Hypertext Markup Language&quot;&gt;HTML&lt;/abbr&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>field-sizing</b> = <b>none</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>abbr { field-sizing: none; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">What does this selector do? “ALL following siblings.”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>✔ A. <code>~</code></li><li>B. <code>*</code></li><li>C. <code>[attr*=…]</code></li><li>D. <code>:nth-of-type(n)</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p1791">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 1792 / 8000 · Practice 5</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p1793">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p1793" data-page="1793" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 916"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 5</span><span>Page 1793 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 916 — var × animation-delay</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">var</span> <span class="badge prop">animation-delay</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">animation-delay</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;var&gt;</code> — a variable in a math expression or program, or a user agent string. Delay before the first cycle starts.</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;var&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><p style="margin:0;font-size:13px">price = <var style="font-style:italic;font-family:monospace">rate</var> × <var style="font-style:italic;font-family:monospace">qty</var></p></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;p&gt;&lt;code&gt;price = &lt;var&gt;rate&lt;/var&gt; × &lt;var&gt;qty&lt;/var&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/p&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>animation-delay</b> = <b>time</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>var { animation-delay: time; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">What does this selector do? “The very first letter of a block.”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>✔ A. <code>::first-letter</code></li><li>B. <code>#id</code></li><li>C. <code>:focus</code></li><li>D. <code>:empty</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p1792">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 1793 / 8000 · Practice 5</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p1794">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p1794" data-page="1794" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 917"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 5</span><span>Page 1794 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 917 — bdo × scale</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">bdo</span> <span class="badge prop">scale</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">scale</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;bdo&gt;</code> — forces the visual direction of text (use sparingly). Independent scale (composes with transform).</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;bdo&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><p style="margin:0;font-size:13px"><bdo dir="rtl" style="background:#fee2e2;padding:0 4px;border-radius:3px">12:30</bdo> — forced RTL rendering</p></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;bdo dir=&quot;rtl&quot;&gt;12:30 → 03:21&lt;/bdo&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>scale</b> = <b>…</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>bdo { scale: …; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">What does this selector do? “The placeholder text inside inputs.”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>✔ A. <code>::placeholder</code></li><li>B. <code>[attr^=…]</code></li><li>C. <code>:first-child</code></li><li>D. <code>:where(sel, …)</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p1793">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 1794 / 8000 · Practice 5</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p1795">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p1795" data-page="1795" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 918"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 5</span><span>Page 1795 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 918 — img × aspect-ratio</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">img</span> <span class="badge prop">aspect-ratio</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">aspect-ratio</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;img&gt;</code> — embeds an image. Locks the width:height ratio (16/9, 1/1, 4/3…).</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;img&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><div style="width:130px;height:86px;border-radius:8px;background:radial-gradient(circle at 30% 30%,#fbbf24,#92400e);position:relative;overflow:hidden"><span style="position:absolute;bottom:4px;right:6px;font-size:10px;color:#fff;text-shadow:0 1px 2px #000">cat.jpg 400×260</span></div></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;img src=&quot;cat.jpg&quot; alt=&quot;A cat sleeping on a laptop&quot; width=&quot;400&quot;&gt; &lt;img srcset=&quot;cat-400.jpg 400w, cat-800.jpg 800w&quot; sizes=&quot;(max-width: 600px) 90vw, 400px&quot;&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>aspect-ratio</b> = <b>auto</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>img { aspect-ratio: auto; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">What does this selector do? “The button part of &lt;input type=&quot;file&quot;&gt;.”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>A. <code>:</code></li><li>✔ B. <code>::file-selector-button</code></li><li>C. <code>:nth-child(n)</code></li><li>D. <code>:enabled / :disabled</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p1794">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 1795 / 8000 · Practice 5</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p1796">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p1796" data-page="1796" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 919"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 5</span><span>Page 1796 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 919 — svg × padding-inline</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">svg</span> <span class="badge prop">padding-inline</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">padding-inline</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;svg&gt;</code> — scalable vector graphics written inline in html. Logical left+right padding (flips with direction).</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;svg&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><svg viewBox="0 0 40 40" width="56" height="56" aria-hidden="true"><circle cx="20" cy="20" r="18" fill="#4285f4"></circle><path d="M12 21 L18 27 L29 14" stroke="#fff" stroke-width="4" fill="none" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"></path></svg></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;svg viewBox=&quot;0 0 40 40&quot; width=&quot;40&quot; height=&quot;40&quot; aria-hidden=&quot;true&quot;&gt; &lt;circle cx=&quot;20&quot; cy=&quot;20&quot; r=&quot;18&quot; fill=&quot;#4285f4&quot;&gt;&lt;/circle&gt; &lt;path d=&quot;M12 21 L18 27 L29 14&quot; stroke=&quot;#fff&quot; stroke-width=&quot;4&quot; fill=&quot;none&quot; stroke-linecap=&quot;round&quot; stroke-linejoin=&quot;round&quot;&gt;&lt;/path&gt; &lt;/svg&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>padding-inline</b> = <b>length</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>svg { padding-inline: length; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">Which is a valid value of box-sizing?</p><ul class="quiz"><li>A. <code>content-box</code></li><li>B. <code>solid2</code></li><li>✔ C. <code>border-box</code></li><li>D. <code>auto2</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p1795">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 1796 / 8000 · Practice 5</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p1797">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p1797" data-page="1797" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 920"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 5</span><span>Page 1797 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 920 — area × box-shadow</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">area</span> <span class="badge prop">box-shadow</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">box-shadow</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;area&gt;</code> — a clickable region (shape + coordinates) inside a &lt;map&gt;. One or more shadows around the box.</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;area&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><div style="font-family:monospace;font-size:11px;background:#f6f8fa;border:1px solid #d0d7de;border-radius:6px;padding:8px">shape=rect coords=0,0,100,50 → /a</div></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;map name=&quot;m&quot;&gt; &lt;area shape=&quot;rect&quot; coords=&quot;0,0,100,50&quot; href=&quot;/a&quot; alt=&quot;Section A&quot;&gt; &lt;/map&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>box-shadow</b> = <b>multiple</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>area { box-shadow: multiple; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">Which is a valid value of border-style?</p><ul class="quiz"><li>✔ A. <code>none</code></li><li>B. <code>hidden</code></li><li>C. <code>always</code></li><li>D. <code>banana2</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p1796">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 1797 / 8000 · Practice 5</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p1798">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p1798" data-page="1798" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 921"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 5</span><span>Page 1798 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 921 — datalist × overflow-wrap</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">datalist</span> <span class="badge prop">overflow-wrap</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">overflow-wrap</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;datalist&gt;</code> — a list of suggestions an &lt;input&gt; can autocomplete from. Break long words so they don&#x27;t overflow (break-word).</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;datalist&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><div style="font-size:12px;max-width:180px"><div style="border:1px solid #d1d5db;border-radius:6px;padding:6px 8px;color:#9ca3af">Bro▮</div><div style="border:1px solid #d1d5db;border-top:none;border-radius:0 0 6px 6px;background:#fff;font-size:11px"><div style="padding:4px 8px">Chrome</div><div style="padding:4px 8px">Firefox</div></div></div></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;input list=&quot;browsers&quot; placeholder=&quot;Browser…&quot;&gt; &lt;datalist id=&quot;browsers&quot;&gt; &lt;option value=&quot;Chrome&quot;&gt; &lt;option value=&quot;Firefox&quot;&gt; &lt;option value=&quot;Safari&quot;&gt; &lt;/datalist&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>overflow-wrap</b> = <b>normal</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>datalist { overflow-wrap: normal; &lt;tr&gt;&lt;th scope=&quot;col&quot;&gt;Name&lt;/th&gt;&lt;th scope=&quot;col&quot;&gt;Score&lt;/th&gt;&lt;/tr&gt; &lt;tr&gt;&lt;th scope=&quot;row&quot;&gt;Ali&lt;/th&gt;&lt;td&gt;92&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt; &lt;tr&gt;&lt;th colspan=&quot;2&quot;&gt;Top scorer: Ali&lt;/th&gt;&lt;/tr&gt; &lt;/table&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>grid-area</b> = <b>name</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>th { grid-area: name; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">Which CSS property: “Where long words may break.”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>✔ A. <code>word-break</code></li><li>B. <code>content</code></li><li>C. <code>aspect-ratio</code></li><li>D. <code>flex-grow</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p1907">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 1908 / 8000 · Practice 6</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p1909">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p1909" data-page="1909" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 1032"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 6</span><span>Page 1909 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 1032 — td × grid-template</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">td</span> <span class="badge prop">grid-template</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">grid-template</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;td&gt;</code> — a standard data cell. }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">Which CSS property: “Filters what is BEHIND the element (glassmorphism!).”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>A. <code>animation-name</code></li><li>B. <code>float</code></li><li>✔ C. <code>backdrop-filter</code></li><li>D. <code>font-style</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p1916">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 1917 / 8000 · Practice 6</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p1918">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p1918" data-page="1918" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 1041"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 6</span><span>Page 1918 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 1041 — em × transform-origin</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">em</span> <span class="badge prop">transform-origin</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">transform-origin</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;em&gt;</code> — marks stress emphasis — change in meaning if removed. The point transforms rotate/scale around.</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;em&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><p style="margin:0;font-size:13px">I love <em>you</em>. — <i>em changes who is stressed</i></p></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;p&gt;I love &lt;em&gt;you&lt;/em&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>transform-origin</b> = <b>…</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>em { transform-origin: …; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">Which CSS property: “Clip the element with an image/gradient mask (alpha channel).”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>A. <code>animation-delay</code></li><li>✔ B. <code>mask-image</code></li><li>C. <code>top</code></li><li>D. <code>font-stretch</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p1917">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 1918 / 8000 · Practice 6</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p1919">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p1919" data-page="1919" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 1042"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 6</span><span>Page 1919 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 1042 — abbr × max-width</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">abbr</span> <span class="badge prop">max-width</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">max-width</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;abbr&gt;</code> — an abbreviation or acronym, with its expansion in the title attribute. The upper limit of the width.</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;abbr&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><p style="margin:0;font-size:13px"><abbr title="Hypertext Markup Language" style="text-decoration:underline dotted;cursor:help">HTML</abbr> — hover me for the tooltip</p></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;abbr title=&quot;Hypertext Markup Language&quot;&gt;HTML&lt;/abbr&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>max-width</b> = <b>none</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>abbr { max-width: none; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">Which CSS property: “Float content around a non-rectangular shape.”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>A. <code>animation-fill-mode</code></li><li>B. <code>right</code></li><li>C. <code>font-optical-sizing</code></li><li>✔ D. <code>shape-outside</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p1918">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 1919 / 8000 · Practice 6</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p1920">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p1920" data-page="1920" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 1043"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 6</span><span>Page 1920 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 1043 — var × padding-top</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">var</span> <span class="badge prop">padding-top</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">padding-top</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;var&gt;</code> — a variable in a math expression or program, or a user agent string. Merges adjacent table borders into one.</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;bdo&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><p style="margin:0;font-size:13px"><bdo dir="rtl" style="background:#fee2e2;padding:0 4px;border-radius:3px">12:30</bdo> — forced RTL rendering</p></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;bdo dir=&quot;rtl&quot;&gt;12:30 → 03:21&lt;/bdo&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>border-collapse</b> = <b>separate</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>bdo { border-collapse: separate; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">Which CSS property: “Reset a CSS counter to a value.”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>✔ A. <code>counter-reset</code></li><li>B. <code>transform-origin</code></li><li>C. <code>overflow-wrap</code></li><li>D. <code>text-align-last</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p1920">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 1921 / 8000 · Practice 6</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p1922">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p1922" data-page="1922" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 1045"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 6</span><span>Page 1922 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 1045 — img × z-index</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">img</span> <span class="badge prop">z-index</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">z-index</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;img&gt;</code> — embeds an image. Stacking order of positioned elements (higher = on top).</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;img&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><div style="width:130px;height:86px;border-radius:8px;background:radial-gradient(circle at 30% 30%,#fbbf24,#92400e);position:relative;overflow:hidden"><span style="position:absolute;bottom:4px;right:6px;font-size:10px;color:#fff;text-shadow:0 1px 2px #000">cat.jpg 400×260</span></div></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;img src=&quot;cat.jpg&quot; alt=&quot;A cat sleeping on a laptop&quot; width=&quot;400&quot;&gt; &lt;img srcset=&quot;cat-400.jpg 400w, cat-800.jpg 800w&quot; sizes=&quot;(max-width: 600px) 90vw, 400px&quot;&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>z-index</b> = <b>auto</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>img { z-index: auto; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">Which CSS property: “Define the quotation marks used by open-quote/close-quote.”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>A. <code>rotate</code></li><li>✔ B. <code>quotes</code></li><li>C. <code>zoom</code></li><li>D. <code>text-decoration</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p1921">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 1922 / 8000 · Practice 6</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p1923">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p1923" data-page="1923" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 1046"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 6</span><span>Page 1923 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 1046 — svg × flex-wrap</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">svg</span> <span class="badge prop">flex-wrap</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">flex-wrap</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;svg&gt;</code> — scalable vector graphics written inline in html. stroke=&quot;#fff&quot; stroke-width=&quot;4&quot; fill=&quot;none&quot; stroke-linecap=&quot;round&quot; stroke-linejoin=&quot;round&quot;&gt;&lt;/path&gt; &lt;/svg&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>flex-wrap</b> = <b>wrap</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>svg { flex-wrap: wrap; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">Which CSS property: “Padding inside a scroll/snap container (align snapped items under headers).”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>A. <code>height</code></li><li>✔ B. <code>scroll-padding-top</code></li><li>C. <code>align-items</code></li><li>D. <code>word-break</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p1924">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 1925 / 8000 · Practice 6</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p1926">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p1926" data-page="1926" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 1049"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 6</span><span>Page 1926 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 1049 — caption × font-optical-sizing</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">caption</span> <span class="badge prop">font-optical-sizing</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">font-optical-sizing</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;caption&gt;</code> — the title/caption of a &lt;table&gt;. One or more shadows behind the text.</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;th&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><table style="border-collapse:collapse;font-size:11px"><tr><th style="border:1px solid #d1d5db;background:#f3f4f6;padding:4px 10px">Name</th><th style="border:1px solid #d1d5db;background:#f3f4f6;padding:4px 10px">Score</th></tr><tr><th style="border:1px solid #e5e7eb;padding:4px 10px;background:#fafafa">Ali</th><td style="border:1px solid #e5e7eb;padding:4px 10px">92</td></tr><tr><td colspan="2" style="border:1px solid #e5e7eb;padding:4px 10px;background:#eff6ff;font-weight:600">Top scorer: Ali</td></tr></table></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;table&gt; &lt;tr&gt;&lt;th colspan=&quot;2&quot;&gt;Top scorer: Ali&lt;/th&gt;&lt;/tr&gt; &lt;/table&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>text-shadow</b> = <b>…</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>th { text-shadow: …;
